approved: Not-for-profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill 2013

Backed the Not-for-profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill, arguing not-for-profits, of which there are over 600,000 in Australia, should not be treated as instruments of government, and proposed replacing the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission with a smaller advisory body while protecting the sector's ability to advocate on Commonwealth policy.

Introduced the Not-for-Profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill 2013, which would prohibit and invalidate gag clauses in Commonwealth agreements restricting not-for-profit organisations from advocating on government policy, noting the sector comprises around 600,000 organisations and about eight per cent of national employment.

Supported the Not-for-profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill but criticised the government for creating the Australian Charities and Not-for-Profits Commission as an added bureaucratic burden, and pledged a coalition government would transfer its functions to the sector while retaining the common law definition of charity and the public benefit test, consistent with the 2001 charities definition inquiry, the 2008 Henry review and the 2010 Productivity Commission report.

Defended the Not-for-Profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill 2013, accusing Liberal state governments in New South Wales and Queensland of imposing gag clauses on community and legal service organisations, and challenged the Leader of the Opposition to publicly condemn the practice by his state colleagues.
